श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके।

हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव

sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

Speaker: Lord Krishna
Battlefield Context & Narrative Story: Krishna explains how nature (Prakriti) creates all forms, while consciousness (Purusha) experiences them. He proclaims that one who sees the supreme, undying divine presence dwelling equally in all perishable creatures possesses true vision and never degrades their own soul.
Sacred Teaching: The Supreme Soul in this body is also called the observer, the permitter, the sustainer, the enjoyer, the great Lord, and the Supreme Self.
Sanskrit Shloka: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः।।13.23।।
Transliteration: upadraṣhṭānumantā cha bhartā bhoktā maheśhvaraḥ
paramātmeti chāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣhaḥ paraḥ

ya evaṁ vetti puruṣhaṁ prakṛitiṁ cha guṇaiḥ saha
sarvathā vartamāno ’pi na sa bhūyo ’bhijāyate

translation: He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter together with their qualities, in whatever condition he may be, he is not reborn.
